sources.cite: AWS. SageMaker AI Developer Guide: Model quality monitoring
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: model quality jobs compare predictions 'with the actual Ground Truth labels', merging captured data 'with actual labels that you store in an Amazon S3 bucket'. The page says nothing about how late labels arrive; the 30-60 day chargeback delay is scenario data.

sources.cite: AWS. SageMaker AI Developer Guide: Shadow tests
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: SageMaker 'routes a copy of the inference requests to it in real time within the same endpoint. Only the responses of the production variant are returned to the calling application'; shadow responses can be logged 'for offline comparison'.

brief.situation: Monday 09:00. You are the ML engineer for a card issuer's fraud-scoring model, a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint in us-east-2 (Ohio). The fraud desk says chargebacks are climbing, but the drift monitor has reported no violations for weeks. Six weeks ago the issuer started accepting instant-pay wallet transactions.
handover: Model v7 has served since launch 14 months ago. Data capture is on; an hourly data-quality schedule compares captured requests with a baseline.
Fraud labels come from chargebacks, which arrive 30 to 60 days after a transaction.
The fraud desk's target: losses under $90,000 a week. About $400,000 of fraud is attempted a week.
howItWorks: Learner-paced: nothing moves until you act. Investigate, change the monitoring and the model, then run the week.
The board shows what is serving and what is watching it; the meters show recall and the projected weekly losses.
Before you run the week you are asked what caused the miss and what you changed. The debrief scores what you did.

source.note: Fraud attempted a week, in dollars.

v8 trained on the last 30 days only: recent fraud is still labeled legitimate because chargebacks have not arrived, so it learns to pass wallet fraud.

whyQ.title: Why no violations?
whyQ.context: The inputs have shifted this far, yet the hourly monitor reported nothing for weeks. Why?

choices.label: Its baseline was rebuilt from production traffic that had already drifted, so the drift became 'normal'
choices.feedback: Right. A baseline should come from data the model is known to be good on, usually its training set; rebuilding it from recent traffic hides the drift.

choices.label: Data-quality monitoring cannot see a new category value
choices.feedback: No. A new value or a shifted distribution is exactly what the comparison catches, against the right baseline.

plan.question: Before you run the week: why did the monitor miss the drift, what did you change, and how are you making sure a new model is better before it serves?

parts.label: The cause
parts.criteria: Names data drift (wallet transactions, shifted amounts) as the cause of the recall drop; explains the silent monitor by a baseline rebuilt from drifted production traffic; rebuilds the baseline from the training data.
parts.modelAnswer: Wallet transactions are 18% of traffic and never appeared in training, so recall fell from 0.84 to 0.61. The monitor stayed quiet because its baseline was rebuilt from recent production traffic, which already contained the drift. The baseline now comes from the training set, with drift alarms to the on-call.

parts.label: The fix and the check
parts.criteria: Retrains on enough history with labels that are complete, holding out the recent weeks whose chargebacks have not arrived; tests the new model as a shadow variant before promoting it.
parts.modelAnswer: Retrain on 15 months but leave out the last 60 days, whose fraud is still labeled legitimate. Run v8 as a shadow beside v7 and promote it only if the fraud desk's confirmed cases show it catches more without more false declines.

expertPath.text: Monitoring report (quiet), then the evidence: traffic against training statistics (wallet transactions are new) and labeled quality (recall 0.61, labels 30-60 days late).
Rebuild the baseline from the training data and alarm on the drift metrics. Retrain on 15 months, holding out the last 60 days whose labels are incomplete.
Deploy v8 as a shadow variant; promote on Thursday after the fraud desk confirms it catches more. The trade-off: three more days at v7's losses for the certainty that v8 is better.

worse.headline: A worse model shipped
worse.body: The newest data looks most like today's traffic, but its fraud is still labeled legitimate until chargebacks arrive. Trained on it, v8 learned to pass wallet fraud, and replacing v7 without a shadow test put it straight into production.

fixed.headline: Drift caught and fixed safely
fixed.body: You confirmed the drift and the label delay first, fixed the monitor's baseline, retrained on mature labels and proved v8 in shadow before it served. That is the expert path.

partly.headline: Better, by a rougher route
partly.body: Check whether you looked at the evidence before changing things, whether the baseline is the training set, whether v8's labels were mature, and whether v8 ran in shadow before serving.

time_up.headline: No decision
time_up.body: The model keeps missing wallet fraud while nothing changes.

scoring.modelReasoning: A monitor compares live inputs with a baseline, so the baseline must come from data the model is known to be good on, normally its training set. Rebuilt from recent production traffic, it absorbs the drift and reports nothing. Here wallet transactions are new to the model and recall fell from 0.84 to 0.61. Ground-truth labels for fraud come from chargebacks 30 to 60 days late, so the newest data is mislabeled: retrain on a long window and hold the immature weeks out. Then test the new model as a shadow variant, which scores copies of live requests without answering them, and promote it only when confirmed cases show it is better. Model Monitor is closed to new customers; a new team builds the same check with the open-source SageMaker AI monitoring solutions and CloudWatch.
